subject: Polity
topic: Attorney General of India — mixed tiers
description: Article 76, appointment, qualifications, tenure, AG vs Solicitor General, parliamentary rights

questions.stem: The Attorney General of India is appointed under which Article of the Constitution?

options.option_text: Article 76, providing for the office of the Attorney General
Article 165, providing for the office of state Advocate General
Article 124, providing for the Supreme Court of India
Article 280, providing for the Union Finance Commission

questions.explanation: Article 76 — Attorney General of India (AGI). Appointed by the PRESIDENT. Highest law officer in India. Must be qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court (5 years HC judge OR 10 years HC advocate OR distinguished jurist). Holds office at the pleasure of the President; not a fixed-term appointment. Article 165 — Advocate General of state (parallel office at state level). Article 124 — Supreme Court. Article 280 — Finance Commission. Current AG (2025): R. Venkataramani.

questions.stem: The Attorney General of India holds office:

options.option_text: For a fixed tenure of 5 years from date of appointment
During the pleasure of the President of India
Until the age of 65 like a Supreme Court judge
Until the next general election to the Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: AGI's tenure — NOT FIXED in the Constitution; holds office during the 'pleasure of the President' (effectively the Cabinet). May resign; may be removed any time. Conventionally, AG resigns when the government changes (since the AG is seen as the Centre's lawyer). Salary + emoluments — fixed by the President. AG has the right to AUDIENCE in any court in India, and to participate in Parliamentary proceedings (without right to vote). The AG can engage in private legal practice (but cannot represent against the government).

questions.stem: The Attorney General has the right to:

options.option_text: Vote on bills as an ordinary member of Parliament
Speak in either House but not vote on any motion
Initiate prosecutions in trial courts as the prosecutor
Override decisions of the Supreme Court of India

questions.explanation: Article 88 — gives AG the right to speak and take part in proceedings of EITHER HOUSE OF PARLIAMENT, joint sitting, and any committee — but WITHOUT THE RIGHT TO VOTE. Same applies to ministers. AG attends to assist Parliament on legal matters. Distractor 1 — AG is not an MP. Distractor 3 — prosecutions are by police / state prosecutors / Public Prosecutors. Distractor 4 — AG cannot override SC.

questions.stem: The first Attorney General of independent India (post-1950) was:

options.option_text: C.K. Daphtary, a noted constitutional lawyer of his era
M.C. Setalvad, who served from 1950 to 1963 in the role
Niren De, a famed Bengali advocate of his generation
Soli Sorabjee, the eminent jurist of his time

questions.explanation: Motilal Chimanlal SETALVAD (1884-1974) — first AG of India, 28 January 1950 to 1 March 1963 (longest-serving AG, ~13 years). Earlier the first Advocate General of Bombay. Headed the First Law Commission of India. Gave the Hamlyn Lectures (Cambridge) — the only Indian to do so. Distractor 1 — C.K. Daphtary was the SECOND AG (1963-68). Distractor 3 — Niren De was AG during the Emergency, infamous for the Habeas Corpus case (ADM Jabalpur). Distractor 4 — Soli Sorabjee was AG twice (1989-90 and 1998-2004).

questions.stem: The SOLICITOR GENERAL of India is:

options.option_text: A constitutional officer ranked above the Attorney General
A statutory officer who assists the AG and represents the state in courts
A judicial officer in the Supreme Court like a registrar
A spokesperson appointed by the Bar Council of India directly

questions.explanation: Solicitor General (SG) — STATUTORY office (Law Officers (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1972), not constitutional. Assists the AG in representing the Union Government in courts (especially the Supreme Court). Several Additional Solicitors General also assist. AG is the chief; SG and ASGs are subordinate. Current SG (2025): Tushar Mehta. Distractor 1 — wrong; SG is BELOW AG, not above. Distractor 3 — SG is a law officer of the government, not a court official. Distractor 4 — appointed by the central government, not Bar Council.

questions.stem: A key DUTY of the Attorney General is to:

options.option_text: Make laws in Parliament on behalf of the Union Government
Advise the Government on legal matters and represent it in court
Decide criminal appeals in the Supreme Court of India
Run the day-to-day affairs of the Ministry of Law and Justice

questions.explanation: Duties of the AG (Article 76(2) + (3)): (1) Give legal advice to the Centre on matters referred to him; (2) Perform duties of legal character assigned by the President; (3) Discharge functions conferred by the Constitution / law. Specifically — represents Union of India in cases the Government is a party to; appears in references under Article 143 (presidential reference); appears in any case where Union has interest. Distractor 1 — AG is not a legislator. Distractor 3 — AG is not a judge. Distractor 4 — Law Minister runs the Ministry of Law.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Attorney General?

options.option_text: The AG is appointed by the President of India under Article 76
The AG must be a member of either House of Parliament to qualify
The AG can take part in Parliament without right to vote
The AG can engage in private legal practice as well, with limits

questions.explanation: AG does NOT need to be a member of Parliament — he is not an MP. Distractor 1 — TRUE: appointment by President under Article 76. Distractor 3 — TRUE: Article 88 right to speak in either House without vote. Distractor 4 — TRUE: AG can practise privately but cannot appear AGAINST the Government, advise persons whose interest may conflict with the Government, or represent in criminal cases without permission.
